scope: SHIP verdict for the develop -> main PR that promotes release 0.4.6, naming develop's current tip 9c3fc0f8a05825d462b6197468fb1719ef726307 (DADAIA.md §4.2: the ship-PR verdict names develop's tip and is staged on the feature branch before the final rc merge; it is staged here as the last commit on feature/0.4.6, so the merged tip's first parent is the named sha and the two-hop verdict store resolves it). Diff-based review of exactly what ships: origin/main fe04319a436b800e895fc4b6c7e1dbb51906611f..origin/develop 9c3fc0f8 = 469 files, +10,570/-18,749; production subtree dadaia_workspace/ = 234 files, +4,269/-12,084 (net -7,815). Lanes run: OWASP/CWE read of the production diff with a path-containment, symlink, subprocess/shell, deletion-path, deserialization and registration-seam lens (features/spec_context/doctor.py, features/spec_context/service.py, features/spec_context/scoped_law.py, features/import_/service.py, features/export/service.py, infrastructure/git_subprocess.py, hooks/pre_gate.py, hooks/root_whitelist.py, hooks/sdd_post_gate.py, features/chokepoints/); secret/private-path/token grep over all 11,024 added lines of the range; dependency delta review plus pip-audit over the shipped lockfile; public-asset privacy scan; IaC/workflow review of .github/workflows/release.yml and the range's CI delta; ship preconditions (pyproject version vs PyPI lineage, absence of tag v0.4.6); bug-ledger reading over the range for the operator's bug-surface standing order.
verdict_reason: No CRITICAL, HIGH or MEDIUM finding is open in the production diff, and the ship preconditions hold. Dependency lane: the lockfile delta is one package — mistune 3.3.2 -> 3.3.4 (declared `mistune = ">=3.0,<4.0"`, sha256 hashes present for both wheel and sdist) — with 76 locked packages on both sides and no package added or removed; pip-audit over the shipped lockfile (74 of 76 pinned packages; pywin32==312 and pyyaml-ft==8.0.0 are excluded by platform/python-version, not by choice) reports `No known vulnerabilities found`. Secrets/privacy lane: 0 secret-assignment hits, 0 `BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY` headers, 0 AWS/GitHub/Slack/OpenAI/JWT token shapes across all 11,024 added lines; the six hits of the local-path/hostname pattern are all the literal filename `.claude/settings.local.json` in the new instance-exceptions tests and its docstring, plus one occurrence of the pattern list itself quoted inside the predecessor verdict's `detail_md` — no real path, IP or hostname; `dadaia public doctor` reports `[ok] public-privacy`, and an independent recursive grep of `dadaia_workspace/public/` for private repo names, operator identity, hosts and RFC1918 addresses returns one false positive (the public asset filename `public/data/dadaia-AGENTS.md` matching case-insensitively). Chokepoints: on the tree as pushed (before this verdict is staged) `dadaia ci push-gate-check` exits 0 in both pre-push ref-line shapes with branch policy, specs-canon and denylist all reached and clean, and `dadaia specs doctor` reports 0 errors / 19 SPEC-DOC-041 archive warnings (pre-existing, warning-only D15); once THIS file is committed both flip to a refusal on this one path — the ship-PR verdict shape the law itself mandates — which is recorded as the LOW CWE-841 finding below, with the denylist/privacy step reached and clean in every run and the CI `verdict-check` gate PASSING; `infrastructure/privacy_check.py`, `features/chokepoints/push_gate.py` and `features/chokepoints/verdict.py` are byte-unchanged in the range, so the publication-boundary defence ships exactly as reviewed on main. Production read: the range's new deletion engine is contained by construction — `doctor._remove` (doctor.py:593-609) resolves the entry's PARENT and rebuilds the location as `parent.resolve() / target.name`, refuses anything not `relative_to(workspace_root.resolve())`, and tests `is_symlink()` BEFORE `is_dir()` so a symlinked entry is unlinked and never followed into; `_entries` (doctor.py:305-314) returns `[]` for a symlinked root so no walk crosses a redirected zone; `_remove_dead_repo` (doctor.py:532-543) refuses any `repos/<slug>` whose `resolve().parent` is not `repos/` and re-reads DEAD state at the moment of deletion; `_guarded` (doctor.py:545-554) turns every OSError into one skip line so the reaper never aborts mid-pass. The candidate-4 security HIGH is fixed structurally, not patched: `SpecContextService.register` (service.py:171-198) is the ONE registry insert, allowlisting the context name and every slug through `CONTEXT_NAME_RE.fullmatch` (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`, so `..`, `.`, path separators and empty are all refused) before anything is written, and `dadaia import` reaches the store only through that seam (`ImportService.__init__` takes a `ContextRegistry` Protocol; the service never writes the store). `import` deserializes JSON only, with a pinned `schema_version` and shape checks (`import_/service.py:29-45`) — no pickle, yaml, eval, exec, tarfile or zipfile appears anywhere in the added production lines, and no `shell=True`/`os.system` call is added. `scoped_law.install_scoped_law` writes every row through a single atomic `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY|O_NOFOLLOW` open and skips a symlinked repo or parent (CWE-59/CWE-367). `GitSubprocessClient.clone` still refuses `ext::` URLs and any URL starting with `-` (RCE and argument injection) and builds argv as a list, never a shell string. IaC/workflow: `.github/workflows/release.yml` is unchanged in the range and publishes on push to main behind the `release-gate` environment then the `pypi` environment via `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` pinned by commit sha, using OIDC trusted publishing — top-level `permissions: contents: read`, the publish job narrowing to `contents: write` + `id-token: write`, with no `secrets.PYPI_*`, no `__token__`, no static credential anywhere in the file; every `uses:` in the file is sha-pinned. Ship preconditions: `pyproject.toml` version is 0.4.6 = PyPI latest 0.4.5 + 1 patch (ADR 0005), and no tag `v0.4.6` exists locally (`git tag -l`) or on origin (`git ls-remote --tags`), so the publish job fires exactly once on merge. Bug-surface verdict (operator standing order): the range REDUCES the bug surface, and the evidence is deletion-shaped rather than additive. `git log origin/main..origin/develop -- specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl` shows 54 ledger commits over 20 `fix(...)` commits; the diff adds 13 `resolved` records against 3 new `open` LOW records, and the three HIGH resolutions are all structural single-seam collapses, not branches — `import-registers-unvalidated-slugs-that-doctor-fix-inv5-rmtrees` (one guarded `register` seam replacing scattered inserts, plus the INV-5 containment predicate), `doctor-walks-symlinked-zone-root-into-a-repo-tree` (one `_entries` refusal replacing a per-entry guard that only checked the target), and the third landing in the same seam family. Production is 234 files at +4,269/-12,084, a net -7,815 lines with 89 production files deleted and four whole features retired (`reports/retention`, `tmp_gc`, `academy`, `workspace_clean`) plus `infrastructure/jsonl_log_rotation.py`, the panel Reports/Academy views, `core/models/hygiene.py` and eight `reports` CLI verbs; `setup.cfg` correspondingly loses three independence modules, two CLI source modules and one `ignore_imports` exemption — the architecture contract got smaller, not looser. The doctor consolidation collapsed four GC reapers and three name lists into one registry (`core/workspace_layout.DADAIA_ZONES`) and one scan, and `hooks/pre_gate.py` lost 47 lines of latency telemetry without gaining a branch. Residual risk is four LOW items (three in the shipped code, one in the push mechanics of this very verdict), all reproducible from this report, none of them an auth, injection, crypto or exposure defect on a production-facing path: two are carried forward and re-verified against origin/develop (CWE-706 `--workspace` ancestor walk, already registered and open; CWE-59/61 symlinked zone root classified `canon`, inert on the read side), and one is new to this range's export rewrite (CWE-522 `repo_url` copied verbatim into the portable `.dadaia/dist/spec-contexts.json`), verified against the live registry as carrying no credential today: 11 URLs, 0 with userinfo.

findings.message: CWE-706 — `dadaia import --workspace <path>` and `dadaia export --workspace <path>` re-resolve an explicit path through the ancestor walk and can act on a PARENT workspace (cli/commands/import_.py:30, cli/commands/export.py:29 -> core/workspace_resolver.py ancestor loop). Carried forward from the efd58d33 verdict; re-verified unchanged at origin/develop; registered and open.
findings.detail_md:
`import` and `export` both call `container.build_*_service(resolve_workspace_root(workspace))`. `resolve_workspace_root` walks `[start, *start.parents]` and returns the first ancestor holding `.dadaia/states/spec_contexts.json`; it never applies the `.dadaia/` boundary that `resolve_workspace_root_for_init(explicit=True)` added for the resolved HIGH `ancestor-walk-workspace-root-silent-mistarget` (that fix was scoped to `init` + `reports validate`, which is the verb-local shape that lets the same symptom reappear on a new verb pair).

Reproduced by the predecessor review (not re-run here, to avoid mutating the live registry): `dadaia import --workspace <an uninitialized dir nested under the live workspace> <file>` exited 0 and registered records in the LIVE workspace registry; the effect was reverted with `dadaia context delete`.

Impact is bounded, and this range is what bounds it: every insert now passes `SpecContextService.register` (service.py:171-198), so only allowlisted, unowned slugs land, as DEAD records, with nothing written to disk. Registered as `import-export-workspace-flag-re-resolves-through-ancestor-walk` (LOW, open, reported_by security-reviewer, redacted).
findings.fix_recommendation: Arm B, non-blocking for the ship. Deletion-shaped structural fix: ONE resolver that treats an explicit `--workspace` path as authoritative (raise `WorkspaceNotInitializedError` when it lacks the sentinel) and applies the `.dadaia/` boundary for every verb; delete the init-only `resolve_workspace_root_for_init` variant so the rule has one home. RED test: `import --workspace <uninitialized dir nested under a workspace's .dadaia/tmp>` must exit 1 and write nothing to the parent registry.

findings.message: CWE-59/CWE-61 — a symlinked zone root (e.g. `.dadaia/handoff -> ../repos/<victim>`) is classified `canon` and never surfaced: `_scan_dadaia_top` (features/spec_context/doctor.py:390) tests `entry.is_dir()`, which follows the link. Carried forward from the efd58d33 verdict; re-verified unchanged at origin/develop.
findings.detail_md:
Inert on the read and write sides, which is why it is LOW and not higher: `_entries` (doctor.py:305-314) returns `[]` for a symlinked directory, so no walk ever crosses the link; `_remove` (doctor.py:593-609) tests `is_symlink()` before `is_dir()`, so a symlinked entry is unlinked rather than followed. The predecessor reproduced the end state on a scratch workspace: `dadaia doctor --json` with `.dadaia/handoff -> ../repos/victim` produced `issues: []` and no finding naming the target's contents, and `--fix --expired-only` (the SessionStart lane) left both the link and the target intact.

Residual risk is reporting, not deletion: a redirected zone root is reported as canonical, so the operator's one workspace scan states a false clean, and any later reader that trusts the zone path (`--fix` seeding, a future zone-level operation, any writer) inherits the redirection silently. The bug-history reading matters here — `doctor-walks-symlinked-zone-root-into-a-repo-tree` was fixed IN this range by adding the `_entries` refusal, which closed the walk but left the classification branch untouched.
findings.fix_recommendation: Non-blocking. In `_scan_dadaia_top`, classify `entry.is_symlink()` as SLOP with detail `(symlink)` so `--fix` routes it through `_remove`, which unlinks a symlink and never follows it — one branch on an existing classification chain, no new code path. Pin by extending the existing `test_a_symlinked_zone_root_is_never_walked` parametrization to assert exactly one `WS-dadaia-slop` finding on the zone entry.

findings.message: CWE-522/CWE-532 — `dadaia export` copies `repo_url` and every associated repo `url` verbatim into `.dadaia/dist/spec-contexts.json` (features/export/service.py `_record`), with no userinfo stripping and no warning; that file is the portable artifact intended to be carried to another machine, so a credential-bearing clone URL (`https://user:token@host/org/repo.git`) would be persisted into a generated config. NEW in this range (the export service is rewritten here). No live credential today: the live registry holds 11 URLs, 0 with userinfo.
findings.detail_md:
`ExportService.run` builds `{"slug", "name", "state", "repo_url", "branch", "associated_repos": [{"slug", "url"}], "last_sync_at"}` per context and `atomic_write`s the payload to `<workspace>/.dadaia/dist/spec-contexts.json`. `repo_url` is never validated or normalized on the way in either: `context create`, `repo add`, `update_url` and the `_backfill_repo_url` path (which reads the on-disk `origin` remote, the most likely place a token-bearing URL enters) all store the string as given, and `register` allowlists only the name and slugs, never the URL.

Why this is LOW and not MEDIUM: it materializes only where the operator already embedded a credential in a clone URL; the same string is already at rest in `.dadaia/states/spec_contexts.json` on the same disk; and `.dadaia/` is never committed. Why it is a finding at all: DADAIA.md §9 states credential material lives in exactly one place (the root `.env`) and is never copied into a generated config, and `dist/` is the one export artifact whose whole purpose is to leave the machine — unlike `states/`, it carries no TTL and no reaper. Verified against the live workspace with a count-only, value-free check: 11 URLs in the registry, 0 matching `^[a-z]+://[^/@]*@` — no value was read, printed or stored by this review.

Related hardening already present and unchanged, which is why the exposure stops at disclosure and does not reach execution: `GitSubprocessClient.clone` refuses `ext::` URLs and any URL starting with `-`, and builds argv as a list, so an imported URL cannot become a git option or an arbitrary remote helper.
findings.fix_recommendation: Non-blocking, deletion-shaped. Strip the userinfo component when a URL is written to `dist/`: one helper applied in `_record` that rewrites `scheme://user:token@host/...` to `scheme://host/...`, so the export is portable by construction rather than by operator vigilance. Pin with a unit test asserting a registry entry whose `repo_url` carries userinfo exports without it. Optionally reject userinfo at the `register`/`update_url` boundary so the registry never holds one — that is the version with the smaller surface.

findings.message: CWE-841 — the ship-PR verdict shape the law mandates is refused by two of this project's own chokepoints: staging this file on feature/0.4.6 (DADAIA.md §4.2, dd-gitflow-default §3b) makes `dadaia ci push-gate-check` exit 1 and `dadaia specs doctor` report a SPEC-DOC-044 error, with `--fix` offering to DELETE the required evidence. Second symptom of the in-range bug `verdict-check-head-or-first-parent-cannot-be-satisfied-by-a-develop-to-main-pr`, whose fix (0b8a67d1) taught only `verdict-check` the ship shape.
findings.detail_md:
Reproduced on a dangling `git commit-tree` (V = 90d6aee1753c69f4bac1d0dff0b5e22ae14db22d, parent e8ddf085, tree = HEAD plus both verdict files; no ref moved, nothing committed):

- `dadaia ci push-gate-check` with `refs/heads/feature/0.4.6 V refs/heads/feature/0.4.6 9c3fc0f8` -> **exit 1**: `[pre-push] BLOCKED: the pushed range publishes 1 specs/ path(s) violating the v6 canon or the verdict rule (DADAIA.md §6)` naming `specs/releases/0.4.6/verdicts/9c3fc0f8...handoff.json — delete the path`. Same exit 1 with a zero remote sha.
- `dadaia specs doctor --json` -> one `severity: error`, `code: SPEC-DOC-044`, on the same path: `its sha is neither the branch head (e8ddf08519af) nor its first parent (6057c6e03d1c). A consumed-or-stale verdict never stays on disk. Auto-fix available (run doctor --fix) to delete it.`
- `dadaia ci verdict-check --head V --release-id 0.4.6` -> **exit 0 PASS**, resolving the sibling e8ddf085 verdict.

The structural cause is a rule with two homes that disagree: `covering_verdict` (features/chokepoints/verdict.py) implements the two-hop head-or-first-parent store and was taught the ship-PR shape by 0b8a67d1, while SPEC-DOC-044 and the push gate's specs-canon scan re-derive the same staleness rule against the FEATURE branch's head/first parent, where a develop-tip sha can never appear. Per DADAIA.md §4.2 the ship verdict must name develop's tip and be staged on the feature branch, so the two validators are unsatisfiable together — by construction, not by mistake in this release.

Why this is a security finding and not merely a workflow annoyance: the only ways forward are `git push --no-verify` (the gate's own sanctioned bypass, which normalises bypassing the chokepoint that also carries the denylist privacy scan) or running an auto-fix that deletes the release's security evidence. Both erode the control that DADAIA.md §3.4 relies on. Severity stays LOW: it is a local process control, no external attacker is involved, the denylist scan itself is reached and clean in every run, and the CI gate that actually blocks the PR (`verdict-check`) is correct.

Bug-history reading (operator standing order): the registered record `verdict-check-head-or-first-parent-cannot-be-satisfied-by-a-develop-to-main-pr` was closed by adding a protocol test for the ship-PR shape to `verdict-check` alone. A fix followed by the same symptom on a second validator is the verb-local signature this workspace has hit before (see the CWE-706 finding above, where an init-only resolver fix left `import`/`export` exposed). The correct fix is deletion-shaped: ONE staleness predicate consumed by `verdict-check`, SPEC-DOC-044 and the push-gate canon scan.
findings.fix_recommendation: Arm B, non-blocking for this ship but blocking for the push mechanics — register it before pushing. Structural fix: extract the single staleness predicate already implemented by `features/chokepoints/verdict.py::covering_verdict` and have SPEC-DOC-044 and the push gate's `_run_specs_canon_scan` call it instead of re-deriving the rule, so a verdict naming develop's tip is valid on the feature branch exactly when the ship-PR shape says it is; delete the duplicated rule from the other two sites. RED test: a feature-branch tree carrying a verdict named for develop's tip must pass `specs doctor` and `push-gate-check` and must still fail for a genuinely stale sha. Interim, for THIS push only: push with `--no-verify` (it leaves a reflog trace) after confirming `push-gate-check`'s denylist step is clean — it is, in every run recorded here — and do not run any `--fix`.

findings.message: Dependency lane — pip-audit over the shipped lockfile reports `No known vulnerabilities found` for 74 of the 76 pinned packages; the lockfile delta is one package, mistune 3.3.2 -> 3.3.4, with sha256 hashes present for both artifacts.
findings.detail_md:
Method: `poetry.lock` at `origin/develop` was converted to `name==version` pins and audited with `pip-audit -r <pins> --no-deps` (exit 0). Two packages are excluded by platform rather than by choice and could not be resolved on this host: `pywin32==312` (no Linux distribution) and `pyyaml-ft==8.0.0` (requires python>=3.13, the free-threading variant); neither is reachable on the Linux/macOS publish path and both are dependency-of-dependency pins.

`pyproject.toml` changes no dependency constraint in the range — only the version bump and two pytest marker help strings; `mistune` stays declared as `>=3.0,<4.0`, so 3.3.4 is inside the published constraint and the lock `content-hash` is unchanged, consistent with an in-range resolver refresh rather than a dependency change. mistune is the markdown renderer behind the panel's memory views; the bump is a patch-level move within a supported line.
findings.fix_recommendation: None for the ship. On the next tooling refresh, re-run the audit from a python>=3.13 environment so `pyyaml-ft` is covered too.

findings.message: Supply-chain integrity note — `poetry.lock` `lock-version` regressed 2.1 -> 2.0 in this range, which dropped several environment-marker lines (`markers = {main = ...}`, `markers = "python_version == \"3.13\""` and similar) while keeping every package, version and artifact hash intact.
findings.detail_md: A `lock-version` going DOWN means the lock was regenerated by an OLDER Poetry than the one that wrote the previous lock (the workspace venv carries poetry 1.8.3, which writes 2.0). No package was added or removed (76 on both sides), no `content-hash` changed and every `files = [{file = ..., hash = "sha256:..."}]` entry survives, so artifact pinning and hash verification are unaffected and this is not an exposure. The risk is drift, not compromise: markers that scope a dependency to a python version or an extra are how a lock stays reproducible across the CI matrix, and losing them can install a package on a platform the previous lock excluded.
findings.fix_recommendation: Record-only for the ship. Pin the Poetry version used to regenerate the lock (a CI check or a documented tooling version) so the lock format only ever moves forward; regenerate with the newer Poetry on the next dependency touch and confirm the marker lines return.

findings.message: Release workflow reviewed and unchanged in the range — `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes on push to main behind the `release-gate` environment and then the `pypi` environment, via OIDC trusted publishing with `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` pinned by commit sha; no static token, no `secrets.PYPI_*`, no `__token__`, and every `uses:` in the file is sha-pinned.
findings.detail_md:
Verified in the file at `origin/develop`: top-level `permissions: contents: read` (least privilege by default); the publish job declares `environment: pypi` and narrows to `permissions: contents: write` + `id-token: write` — `id-token: write` is exactly what OIDC trusted publishing requires and is scoped to the one job that needs it; the approval gate job declares `environment: release-gate`, so the operator's click remains a hard precondition. Every action reference (`actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-python`, `actions/setup-node`, `actions/cache`, `actions/upload-artifact`, `actions/download-artifact`, `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish`) is pinned to a 40-hex commit sha with the version in a trailing comment (CWE-829 mitigated; no mutable tag anywhere).

The range's entire `.github/` delta is two cosmetic lines plus one relaxation: `ci.yml` rewords a flaky-test error message (skill rename), and `.github/scripts/check_no_repo_local_claude.sh` drops `CLAUDE.md` from both the forbidden-tracked regex and the forbidden-root-artefact loop. See the separate INFO on that relaxation.
findings.fix_recommendation: None. Keep the sha-pinning discipline on the next action bump, and keep `release-gate` as a protected environment with the operator as the sole reviewer.

findings.message: CI relaxation reviewed — `check_no_repo_local_claude.sh` no longer forbids a repo-root `CLAUDE.md`, and `.gitignore` no longer ignores `/CLAUDE.md`, so the library repo now tracks its own scoped-law file. Content is one line, `@AGENTS.md`; no private data, and the harness-dir and `.dadaia/` prohibitions are untouched.
findings.detail_md:
Read at `origin/develop`: `git ls-tree origin/develop --name-only` shows `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` at root, and `CLAUDE.md` contains exactly `@AGENTS.md` — the import bridge, carrying no instruction, no path and no operator detail. This is the intended consequence of the range's scoped-law table (`scoped_law.py` `_ROWS` now installs `repo-CLAUDE.md` and `tests-CLAUDE.md` alongside the AGENTS pair, with the new templates added under `public/templates/`), so the source library holds the same scoped law it projects.

The guard that matters is intact: `.claude/`, `.agents/`, `.codex/` and `.dadaia/` remain forbidden both as tracked paths and as existing root entries, so a real local harness projection still fails CI. The residual is that a future hand-edit could put instructions or paths into a now-tracked root `CLAUDE.md` without CI noticing; the `public doctor` privacy check and the pre-push denylist scan remain the controls for that, and both are clean.
findings.fix_recommendation: None for the ship. If the one-line bridge ever grows content, treat it as a public asset under DADAIA.md §8.3 and keep it free of consumer names, hosts and operator paths.

findings.message: Deletion-path containment re-read and confirmed — the range's new `dadaia doctor` reaper resolves the entry's parent (never the target), refuses anything outside the workspace, unlinks symlinks instead of following them, refuses a `repos/<slug>` that does not resolve to a direct child of `repos/`, and skips-and-reports on every OSError instead of aborting the pass.
findings.detail_md:
Evidence at `origin/develop`, `features/spec_context/doctor.py`:

- `_remove` (:593-609): `location = target.parent.resolve() / target.name`; `location.relative_to(self._workspace_root.resolve())` inside a `try`, returning `skipped '<path>' (outside the workspace)` on `ValueError`; then `if target.is_symlink() or target.is_file(): target.unlink()` BEFORE `elif target.is_dir(): shutil.rmtree(target)`. Resolving the parent rather than the target is the correct choice: a symlink is judged by where it LIVES, so a link pointing outside cannot smuggle a deletion, and a parent that itself points outside the workspace fails the containment test.
- `_entries` (:305-314): `if directory.is_symlink(): return []`, with the docstring naming the exact attack it closes — `iterdir` would follow the link and every entry of the target would pass the per-entry guard because its parent is inside the workspace. This is the structural fix for `doctor-walks-symlinked-zone-root-into-a-repo-tree`.
- `_remove_dead_repo` (:532-543): `if repo_path.resolve().parent != self._repos_dir().resolve(): return "skipped ... (outside repos/)"`, then a fresh `self._store.get(ctx.name)` re-read requiring `ContextState.DEAD` at the moment of deletion.
- `_guarded` (:545-554): every step's `OSError` becomes one `skipped '<path>' (errno N: msg)` line, so one undeletable entry cannot abort the pass (the structural fix for `doctor-fix-aborts-whole-pass-on-first-undeletable-entry`).

Residual, record-only: a TOCTOU window exists between `is_symlink()` and `shutil.rmtree` in `_remove`, exploitable only by a local process that can already write inside the workspace — i.e. an attacker who already has the capability the deletion would grant. `shutil.rmtree` does not follow symlinked children on CPython, so the blast radius stays inside the resolved directory.
findings.fix_recommendation: None required. If the TOCTOU residual is ever worth closing, the deletion-shaped form is an fd-based removal (`os.open(..., O_NOFOLLOW)` + `shutil.rmtree(fd)`) on the one seam, not a second validation branch.

findings.message: Registration and deserialization surfaces re-read and confirmed — `SpecContextService.register` is the ONE guarded registry insert (name and every slug allowlisted by `CONTEXT_NAME_RE.fullmatch`), `dadaia import` reaches the store only through it, and the import path deserializes JSON only, with a pinned `schema_version`; no pickle, yaml, eval, exec, tarfile, zipfile or `shell=True` appears in the range's added production lines.
findings.detail_md:
`features/spec_context/service.py:171-198` — `register` calls `_require_allowlisted("context name", ctx.name)`, refuses an existing name, then `_refuse_slug` for the main slug and for every associated repo, additionally refusing a repeat of the main slug and a duplicate within the list; `self._store.save(ctx)` runs only after every check. `_require_allowlisted` (:117-122) applies `CONTEXT_NAME_RE.fullmatch`, and `CONTEXT_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]+")` at `core/models/spec_context.py:10` — `fullmatch` on that class refuses `..`, `.`, `/`, `\`, empty and any embedded newline, which is precisely the input that made `doctor --fix` INV-5 rmtree an unbounded path in the resolved HIGH.

`features/import_/service.py` — `ImportService.__init__` accepts a `ContextRegistry` Protocol (`register` only) wired by the container, so the feature CANNOT write the store directly; `_read` (:29-45) requires a real file, parses with `json.loads`, requires a dict payload whose `schema_version` equals the pinned constant, and requires `contexts` to be a list of dicts; `_dead_context` coerces every field with `str()` and forces `state=ContextState.DEAD`, so an import can never register an ALIVE context or place anything on disk. Refusals from the seam (`InvalidContextNameError`, `AssociatedRepoConflictError`, `ContextAlreadyExistsError`) are caught per record and reported as skips.

`infrastructure/git_subprocess.py:235-244` — `clone` refuses `url.startswith("ext::")` (arbitrary remote helper = RCE) and `url.startswith("-")` (argument injection into `git clone`), then runs `_run(["git", "clone", url, str(dest)])` as a list, never a shell string; the file's other git calls consistently use `--` before pathspecs. This is the control that keeps the unvalidated `repo_url` of the LOW above at disclosure severity rather than execution.

`features/spec_context/scoped_law.py` — all four rows go through one `os.open(dst, O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY|O_NOFOLLOW, 0o644)`, so "already exists", "is a symlink (dangling or not)" and "was swapped mid-window" are a single indivisible refusal (CWE-59/CWE-367); a symlinked repo root or a symlinked parent directory is skipped before the open. The rewrite replaced a `shutil.copy2` branch with the same atomic open the other row already used — one path where there were two.

findings.message: Gate-integrity note — the root-whitelist exception file was RENAMED in this range (`.dadaia/states/root_exceptions.txt` -> `.dadaia/states/instance_exceptions.txt`, now read via `workspace_layout.INSTANCE_EXCEPTIONS` / `parse_exception_globs`); the mechanism is unchanged in kind, including the pre-existing property that the file sits in a MUTATING path class and is therefore agent-writable.
findings.detail_md:
`hooks/root_whitelist.py` `_operator_exception` previously read `<workspace>/.dadaia/states/root_exceptions.txt` and inlined its own strip/comment/fnmatch loop; it now reads `<workspace>/<workspace_layout.INSTANCE_EXCEPTIONS>` and delegates parsing to `workspace_layout.parse_exception_globs`. Same fnmatch semantics on the first path component, same fail-closed `OSError -> False`, one parser instead of two — the change is a consolidation, not a policy move.

The standing property worth stating once: per DADAIA.md §3.2 only `.dadaia/sessions/` and the projected law files are PROTECTED, so `.dadaia/states/` is MUTATING and an agent can append a glob to the exceptions file and thereby widen the root whitelist for itself. That is unchanged by this range and is coherent with DADAIA.md §3.5 — the gate constrains what is written, not who may relax it, and it is workspace discipline rather than a privilege boundary; the controls that ARE security boundaries (the pre-push denylist scan, `privacy_check`, the verdict gate) are untouched in this range. Recorded so the property is on the record rather than assumed.
findings.fix_recommendation: None for the ship. If the operator ever wants the exception list to be operator-only in fact as well as in name, the deletion-shaped move is to classify `.dadaia/states/instance_exceptions.txt` PROTECTED in the one path-class table, not to add a check in the hook.

findings.message: OWASP A09 (logging/monitoring) reviewed for the retirement of hook-latency telemetry and JSONL rotation — the removed writers carried performance timings only; no security-relevant log, audit trail or verdict record was retired, and the auditable trace (git history, `_RELEASE.json` log, `BUGS.jsonl`, verdict files) is unchanged.
findings.detail_md:
`hooks/pre_gate.py` loses `_append_latency` and its `time.monotonic()` wrapper (-47 lines), and `infrastructure/jsonl_log_rotation.py` is deleted (-178) along with `features/telemetry`'s writers; `hooks/sdd_post_gate.py` drops 181 lines. The records these wrote were `{ts, hook, event, duration_ms}` — a performance metric with no actor, no path, no verdict and no security value; the gate's own decision path is untouched (`main` still reads stdin, evaluates, and emits the block/allow envelope) and the telemetry was explicitly fail-open, so it never influenced a verdict. Removing them shrinks the write surface inside `.dadaia/` and removes a rotation code path that was itself a source of bugs.

What remains as the audit trail after the range is exactly what DADAIA.md relies on: git history (commit shapes per `dd-gitflow-default` §3a), `specs/releases/<id>/_RELEASE.json` `log`, `specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl`, the audit histos and the verdict files — none of which this range weakens.

findings.message: Ship preconditions verified — `pyproject.toml` version 0.4.6 = PyPI latest 0.4.5 + 1 patch (ADR 0005), and no tag `v0.4.6` exists locally or on origin, so the merge to main fires the publish exactly once.
findings.detail_md: `git show origin/develop:pyproject.toml` -> `name = "dadaia-workspace"`, `version = "0.4.6"`; the diff against `origin/main` shows `0.4.5 -> 0.4.6` and no other packaging change. `git tag -l 'v0.4.6'` and `git ls-remote --tags origin 'v0.4.6'` both return empty. `dadaia public doctor` additionally reports `[ok] entities-derivation: 9 Personas <-> 9 core sub-agents` and `[ok] model-resolution`, with one `[info] codex:trust-boundary` note that installed codex-cli 0.145.0 has not been live-certified for hook-fire behaviour (last certified 0.144.4) — an environment-level advisory about the operator's local harness version, not a property of what ships, and explicitly backstopped by the git chokepoints which remain independent of any harness hook.
findings.fix_recommendation: Operator: after the merge, confirm the `release-gate` approval and that the publish job ran once. Re-run `dadaia certify`'s codex-live-probe on the next tooling pass to reconfirm the codex trust-boundary claim for 0.145.0.

findings.message: Bug-surface measurement for the operator's standing order — the range resolves 13 ledger records (3 HIGH) against 3 new open LOW records, deletes 89 production files and 4 whole features, and lands at net -7,815 production lines; the HIGH fixes collapse seams rather than adding branches.
findings.detail_md:
Ledger: `git log origin/main..origin/develop -- specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl` = 54 commits across 20 `fix(...)` commits; the diff of added records shows 13 `resolved` (3 HIGH, 6 MEDIUM, 4 LOW) and 3 `open` (all LOW).

The fixes read as structural, which is the test that matters here:

- `import-registers-unvalidated-slugs-that-doctor-fix-inv5-rmtrees` (HIGH) — replaced scattered registry inserts with ONE guarded `register` seam shared by `context create`, `import` and `add_repo`, and added the INV-5 containment predicate. Import's own service shrank +77/-288.
- `doctor-walks-symlinked-zone-root-into-a-repo-tree` (HIGH) — one refusal in `_entries` replacing a per-entry guard that only checked whether the TARGET was inside the workspace.
- `doctor-fix-aborts-whole-pass-on-first-undeletable-entry`, `doctor-scan-raises-when-a-ttl-entry-vanishes-mid-walk`, `doctor-unreadable-install-ledger-classifies-projections-as-slop` — all resolved into the single `_guarded` skip-and-report wrapper rather than three special cases.
- `migrate-v3-backup-lands-in-closed-states-canon`, `doctor-root1-flags-env-that-dadaia-md-9-declares-canonical` — resolved by deriving from the one zone/root registry (`core/workspace_layout`) instead of hand-kept name lists; three such lists were deleted and ratchets now pin table == registry.

Deletion evidence: `features/reports/retention.py` (-447), `cli/commands/reports.py` (-404, eight verbs), `features/panel/views/api_reports.py` (-332) and the panel Reports/Academy assets, `features/tmp_gc/service.py` (-257), `features/academy/**` (-236 plus its knowledge base), `features/workspace_clean/service.py` (-191), `infrastructure/jsonl_log_rotation.py` (-178), `core/models/hygiene.py` (-148). `setup.cfg` loses three independence modules, two CLI source modules and one `ignore_imports` exemption — the layering contract got tighter, not looser, which is the inverse of the puxadinho signature.

Against that, the range adds 18 production files, of which 15 are public skill/template/fixed-section assets and three are code (`core/fixed_sections.py`, `features/specs/candidate.py`, plus the new public data). The three new open LOW records are all reporting-or-consolidation items, none of them a regression introduced by a fix in this range. Verdict on the standing order: the bug surface is REDUCED.
findings.fix_recommendation: Carry the three open LOW records (this verdict's three findings and their registered bug ids) into the next candidate's pick set, where the two carried ones outrank fresh backlog per DADAIA.md §6.7.

decisions_required: BEFORE PUSHING: `dadaia ci push-gate-check` exits 1 and `dadaia specs doctor` reports SPEC-DOC-044 on THIS file once it is committed, because the law stages a develop-tip verdict on the feature branch. The denylist/privacy step is reached and clean in every run. Either land the fix in the LOW CWE-841 finding first, or push this one commit with `git push --no-verify` (traceable in the reflog) — and register the recurrence as a bug either way.

DO NOT run `dadaia specs doctor --fix` or `dadaia doctor --fix` while this verdict is staged: the auto-fix deletes it, which would silently remove the release's ship evidence and fail the develop -> main security-verdict-gate.

Sequencing (dd-gitflow-default §3b): this verdict must be the LAST commit on feature/0.4.6 before the final feature -> develop merge, and nothing else may land on develop in between, so the merge commit's first parent stays 9c3fc0f8 and `covering_verdict` resolves this file on the develop -> main PR.
Operator: approve the `release-gate` environment on the main merge to let the OIDC publish of 0.4.6 proceed; confirm afterwards that the publish job ran exactly once and that tag v0.4.6 now exists.
This verdict is consumed and deleted by the develop -> main merge, like any other (DADAIA.md §4.2/§7.6) — a survivor is slop and will trip SPEC-DOC-044.
Ruling on the new LOW (CWE-522): strip userinfo from `repo_url` when writing `.dadaia/dist/spec-contexts.json`, or reject userinfo at the registry boundary — the second has the smaller surface.
Ruling on the carried LOW (CWE-59/61): classify a symlinked zone root as SLOP in `_scan_dadaia_top`, or accept as record-only for another cycle.
Pin the Poetry version that regenerates `poetry.lock` so `lock-version` only moves forward (2.1 -> 2.0 regression observed in this range).
